files.store.py:
SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE purchases (
  account TEXT NOT NULL,
  request_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  note TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (account, request_key)
);
CREATE TABLE outbox (event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, payload TEXT, sent INTEGER NOT NULL);
"""

def record(db, account, request_key, note):
    with db.transaction():
        event_id = db.insert_purchase(account, request_key, note)
        db.insert_outbox(event_id, {"account": account}, sent=0)
    return event_id

criteria.text: Only the authenticated account with purchase permission may reach storage.
Sessions with expires_at less than or equal to now must be rejected before storage.

Every committed purchase has durable publication intent that remains discoverable after restart until marked sent. At-least-once publication is permitted; exactly-once external delivery is not required.
An absent note becomes the string default; an explicit null remains null through storage and response.
SQLite purchase request-key uniqueness is per account, so independent accounts may reuse keys.
The explicit-null test must assert the null result, so a default string cannot pass as correct null behavior.
notify makes at most three timeout attempts and reports ok false to its caller when all attempts time out.

assumptions: db.transaction atomically commits both inserts or rolls both back; the persisted outbox survives restart and pending_outbox returns every committed sent=0 row. These are supplied adapter guarantees, not independently executed observations.
If bus.send fails or a process stops before mark_sent, the row remains pending. A crash after send before mark_sent may redeliver; this is permitted by ARC-1.

The store injected into checkout adapts store.record; the caller is not its low-level signature. Duplicate checkout-request behavior, hidden adapter idempotency and notification-consumer behavior are unknown and outside this review.
session.expires_at and now share the same supplied integer time unit. SQLite primary-key semantics apply to the shown schema; exact runtime versions are not supplied.
